title: Conditional κ = 0.001587467473762886: an E8 bit word with 420 helpers, c = 0.001653826988 (+4.18% over #510)
body:
**Conditional κ = 793733736881443/(5·10¹⁷) = 0.001587467473762886** with #535's complex supplier (complex-bound; +0.160% over #535's 0.001584931111785787, which is bound by #510's bit c).

This PR adds a bit supplier with **R = 420 helpers**. The best bit words so far have 480 (#503, priced at nine stages by #510) and 489 (#493). Priced by #510's nine-stage whole-residual chain (#463 template, 32 replicas, #442 hosting, #315 engines), unchanged:

**c = 413456747036699736067/(2.5·10²³) = 0.001653826988146798944268** (10⁻²⁴ grid; the next point is rejected).

That is +4.18% over #510's R480 c (0.001587447106092548137108) and 4.01% above #535's complex b, so the bit side no longer binds with any cited complex supplier. #493's eleven-stage chain prices the same word at 0.00164031632456626881922 (+4.78% over #493's R489 in that chain).

Both compositions use the six-level, 47-inequality outer assembly of #493 (the one #510 uses; it reproduces #535's published κ values exactly):

| complex supplier (cited from its receipt) | complex b | κ | binds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **#535** (icekylinx; open) | 1589991533606044174031/10²⁴ | **793733736881443/(5·10¹⁷) = 0.001587467473762886** | complex |
| #531 (icekylinx; merged) | 304013615566499291631/(2·10²³) | 1517760977820331/10¹⁸ = 0.001517760977820331 | complex |

With #531's b nothing changes: main's headline was already complex-bound. Each κ is the same with the nine-stage and the eleven-stage c, because the complex side binds in both. The same pipeline files reproduce #510's R480 c, #493's R489 c, and the published κ values of #535 (0.001584931111785787 with #510's c, bit-bound; 0.001562995248531632 with #493's c, bit-bound) and #531 (0.001517760977820331, complex-bound).

**Concurrent PRs.** When this was prepared, #541 (Dugongue) reported κ = 0.001587212454640692, bit-bound with c = 0.001589735702947999. #542 (rohanarun; draft, physical verification pending) reported κ = 0.001587467473762886, the same complex cap as here, with c = 0.001590005077309866, just above #535's b. This word reaches that cap with c 4.0% above #535's b. The bit side therefore stays non-binding for any complex b below 0.001653.

The PR adds one package, `research/e8-bit-r420/`, with its own path-filtered workflow, and one `.gitattributes` line. No other existing file changes. The package runs on top of main: it uses `research/e8-bit-carrier-skeleton` (#493) and #531's receipt, both pinned by sha256.

### Mechanism: keepers read by targets, then rewritten in phase B

- **Partition.** As in #493: 5 complementary D4 pairs, 30 orthogonal 4-frames, 180 cells, 60 D4 quads, 180 D6 frames.
- **Three registers per cell.** Each source has a home cell, and two carriers copy it into its other two cells. Every cell holds exactly three registers (two line branches and one empty register): 120 sources + 240 carriers + 180 empty registers = 540, so R = 420. The 9 totals sit on dead registers (#503's last-eligible-host rule).
- **Phase A.** Cells deliver two sums to their quads and keep one line, quads apply butterflies, and D6 nodes form o1 = o1 + o2. A D6 that does not host a Q-delivery takes a free keeper of the complementary block.
- **Phase B.**
  1. Each target t reads, at the cell C_t = Φ − {t, x(t)} of its 4-frame, the keeper of C_t. This is a source register holding t's single d-line (120 gates).
  2. The 12 keepers read in a block are exactly the block's 12 sources. They climb to the block's D4 frame, and one invertible F₂ transform per block turns them into the 12 Q-deliveries for the complementary block (477 gates).
  3. Each Q-delivery climbs to its target's host D6 and adds that D6's o1 register (120 gates).
  4. Each target climbs from its cell straight to t⊥ and reads its three needers (120 gates).
- **Cleanup.** The literal reverse, at the full frame, of all 2,661 source and helper gates (2,064 in A, 597 in B).
- **Why it gets below 480.** #493's README bound (R ≥ 480 with phase-A totals) used the fact that no register could both give a target its single d-line and feed the block Q-node. DreamingOfClouds' LP in #493's thread reaches 480 under three hypotheses: three branches per source, two transverse quads per cell, and matching-cell sources feeding the block frame. This word keeps the first two and drops the third. The sources that feed the block frame are the d-single keepers, and a target reads each of them at its cell before the Q-node runs. R = 420 equals #493's other bound for this partition: at least three registers per cell with three branches per source.

### Review point: source registers rewritten in phase B, after targets read them

#493 writes sources only in phase A, and its `interface.py` checks that phase B writes only targets. This word has 597 phase-B source writes: 477 source ← source at block D4 frames, and 120 source ← helper at D6 frames. Every one writes a register a target has already read in phase B. No target feeds a source or helper.

**Lemma.** Let z = (x, s) be the sources and arbitrary helper contents, and y the targets. Assume:

- (H1) no z-destination gate reads a target;
- (H2) D is at frame 0, writes targets and reads helpers;
- (H3) A writes only z, and B interleaves z-only gates with target gates in any order;
- (H4) C is the literal reverse of all z-destination gates at the full frame;
- (H5) the target-to-target part V is the identity.

Then the raw word acts as (z, y) ↦ (U z, y + J x + K s), C acts as U⁻¹, and the whole word acts as (x, s, y) ↦ (x, s, y + J x + (K + N) s), where D adds N s. D is legal at frame 0 and C at the full frame. The proof is an induction over the gates: z evolves by itself, and each target gate adds a combination of the current z = U_k z. The order of z-gates and target reads enters only U and M. It is written out in the package README.

**Reading of #425.** #425's lemma (`PROOF.txt` §3, Zhihao Chen) has one structural hypothesis, "No target may feed a z register". It states the block form for the whole raw A/center/B word and executes U⁻¹ "by reversing and inverting the non-target gates", wherever they occur. So the interleaving is covered by #425's text as written. #493's check (4) was a property of the R489 word, not a hypothesis of #425. The bit-side realization is the role-independent common-label pullback of #472's PROOF.md, written out in #535's `PR510-MUTABLE-SOURCE-CARRYOVER.md`. It does not depend on the order either. Reviewers should confirm this reading.

The package checks the point in four ways:

- `code/xcheck.py` reads only the word. It checks the labels (even unimodular, rank 8), frame legality, and the exact F₂ map on all 660 columns with symbolic helper contents. It then evaluates (H1)–(H5) separately and checks the conclusion term by term: z′ = U z, J = I, K equal to D's helper sets, and C = U⁻¹.
- `code/mutants.py` runs nine negative controls, each rejected:
  - a target feeds a source, and a target feeds a helper (F₂-neutral pairs, caught by H1);
  - a dropped cleanup gate;
  - a corrupted phase-B source write with the cleanup changed alike, so every source is still restored;
  - a phase-B source write moved to the source's own line frame;
  - a single target-to-target read;
  - a corrupted frame-0 preconditioner;
  - a phase-B source write moved before the target read of that register;
  - a cleanup gate moved off the full frame.

  A cancelled pair of target-to-target reads (V = I) is accepted as a positive control.
- #370's stock checker refuses the word, and #493's relaxed copy passes it. #493's `interface.py` refuses it at check (4), as expected.
- The official cohort checkers accept the word. Three record-level mutants aimed at the phase-B source writes are rejected by the five-, nine- and eleven-stage column checkers.

### Checks

`bash research/e8-bit-r420/verify.sh DIR` takes about 105 s here: it passed from fresh copies on Python 3.12 and 3.14. The two controls run in the background.

- **Provenance.**
  - Manifest check.
  - 19 files vendored from #510 (its nine-stage chain, the #463, #443, #442 and #315 files it carries, and #503's R480 word) and 2 receipts from #535, all checked by git blob id.
  - Main's files checked by sha256: #493's package through its own `MANIFEST.sha256`, and #531's receipt.
  - Every cited b checked against its receipt.
- **Rebuild.** The word is rebuilt from the frozen CP-SAT plan and must equal the shipped word.
- **Independent replay and lemma.** `xcheck.py` and the 9 + 1 controls. The R489 and R480 words also pass `xcheck.py`, as the lemma's special case.
- **Official checkers.**
  - Legality at NCOPY = 9: 29,874 records, rank mass 5,112.
  - Five-stage formal columns: 900 columns, prefix payload 100 bits < 104.
  - Nine-stage (`columns_k`, KPAIRS = 4): 1,380 columns, 18/18 omitted-bridge controls rejected.
  - Eleven-stage (KPAIRS = 5): 1,620 columns, 24/24 omitted-bridge controls rejected.
  - The KPAIRS = 2 regression, #370's 6 record mutants, the 3 phase-B record mutants, and Gram determinants with prime witnesses on all 672 frames.
- **Nine-stage price.**
  - #442's programme rediscovers the frozen selection, and all 120,960 residuals are hosted whole with 0 banks.
  - The template, parent audit (17 mutations) and hosted audit (8,603,712 instructions, 16 mutations) pass.
  - Invoice: prefix 189 bits (charged 192), two-level 416 (charged 512), maximum child 42 (2·42² < 64²), row 18,355.
- **Eleven-stage price.**
  - #493's audit files are adapted to R = 420 by the same six edits #503 makes for R480.
  - 36,960 residuals are hosted whole; the audit replays 2,628,912 instructions and rejects 22 mutations.
  - Invoice: prefix 4,710 bits (charged 4,736), three-level 14,185 (charged 14,208), row 19,431 < 20,161. This is larger than #473's 3,456/10,304 and enters only the finite cutoffs; all 47 inequalities pass. The headline uses the nine-stage price.
- **Controls.** These run through the same files: #510's R480 at nine stages and #493's R489 at eleven stages (#493's files unmodified). Every c and κ, and #493's emitted program hash, match their PRs' receipts.
- **Local build.** The C++ checkers were built against an overflow-checked 128-bit stand-in for `boost::multiprecision::cpp_int`. The workflow uses libboost-dev.
- **Repository CI.** Main already carries its own joint-dual pin update: its `research/joint-dual/SOURCE.json` matches main's scripts, and the certificates record that file's hash. So this branch does not carry #318's three files, and it changes no root file apart from `.gitattributes`.

### Retained assumptions

- Every interface that #472's and #510's compositions retain:
  - the all-size bit/Gaussian compiler;
  - the mutable-basis and target-label realization (the review point above);
  - whole-call correlated-helper hosting (#442);
  - compressed windows and restored work;
  - the common grid and tape, precision, row and analytic contracts.
- Complex savings are cited from their PRs' receipts, not rebuilt. #535 is an open PR, so the primary κ also depends on its review.
- The plan is a CP-SAT nomination and the hosting selections are nominations of #442's programme; none is claimed optimal.
- This is a conditional finite construction, not a Lean proof.
